client_secret_env.title: Client secret: in the .env
client_secret_env.help: The client secret is not entered here: it is configured in the backend .env file via the RAG_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET variable (source of truth). Restart the backend after changing it.

local_auth.title: Local login (password)
local_auth.help_enabled: The username / password form is offered on the login page, alongside SSO.
local_auth.help_disabled: Only SSO is offered on the login page. Any local login attempt is rejected by the backend.
local_auth.env_hint: This setting is driven by the RAG_LOCAL_AUTH_DISABLED variable in the .env file (source of truth); it cannot be changed from this page.
local_auth.breakglass: Anti-lockout safeguard: if SSO breaks, set RAG_LOCAL_AUTH_DISABLED=false in the .env and restart the backend to re-enable local login.

procedure.title: Create a Client ID (Keycloak)
procedure.intro: Detailed procedure to create the OIDC client referenced above. Values in angle brackets must be adapted to your deployment.
steps: Open the Keycloak admin console (https://<keycloak>/admin) and sign in with a realm admin account.
Top left, select the target realm (e.g. yoops) — this realm is the one that appears in the Issuer URL.
« General settings » step: Client type = OpenID Connect; Client ID = a short identifier (e.g. rag). This is exactly the value to enter in the « Client ID » field above. Click Next.

« Capability config » step: turn on « Client authentication » (ON → confidential client, a secret is generated); turn on « Standard flow » (Authorization Code Flow); leave the rest at defaults. Click Next.
« Login settings » step — Valid redirect URIs: <RAG_PUBLIC_URL>/auth/callback (e.g. https://rag.example.com/auth/callback).
Valid post logout redirect URIs: <RAG_PUBLIC_URL>/ (the root, with trailing slash).
Web origins: <RAG_PUBLIC_URL> (or the value + to auto-derive from redirect URIs). Click Save.
Client « Credentials » tab → copy the « Client secret ». Paste it into the backend .env file: RAG_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=<secret>, then restart the backend.
Client « Client scopes » tab → verify the openid, email and profile scopes are assigned (default): the user's email must be present in the token, as it determines their identity (owner_id).
Enter the Issuer URL in the field above: https://<keycloak>/realms/<realm> (e.g. https://keycloak.example.com/realms/yoops), then Save the configuration.
procedure.note: After saving, test via the SSO button on the login page. On a redirect_uri error, check that the Valid redirect URI matches <RAG_PUBLIC_URL>/auth/callback exactly.
